newsitem.title: USA: Pakistan wheat tender may not happen - U.S. agent.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan wheat tender may not happen - U.S. agent.

text.p: Indications were reported that Pakistan may decide not to tender for around 100,000 tonnes of soft white wheat on March 16, contrary to talk earlier this week, its U.S. export agent and other U.S. exporters said.

"They (Pakistan) have not issued any tender but right now it looks like they may not issue a tender. No final decision has been given...they could still do it," Pakistan's U.S. export agent, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
Several U.S. exporters said on Friday they believed the once-expected tender would not take place.
"It is not going to happen," one U.S. exporter said.
"I guess they do not need it," another exporter said. "I think they cancelled it yesterday (Thursday)."
Pakistan was expected to tender March 16 for 90,000 to 100,000 tonnes of wheat, probably from the U.S. or Australia, U.S. exporters said earlier this month.
The agent noted that Pakistan was probably calculating several factors which include usage, storage and supplies.

"They are also taking into account the monsoon season in which they will not be taking in any cargo during that time and trying to figure out if they have enough (supply) to carry over," the agent said.
